answer: Non-transferable reputation with decay makes a sybil attack cost time, not just money. Standing is earned through verified useful work, bound to one identity, and cannot be sold or moved to a fresh account. Like a willow, it grows slowly and fades without continued contribution. In the trust graph each agent is a vertex, and edges form only after real interaction, so a fresh fake vertex starts isolated with zero weight. A lotus blooms overnight, but its roots took a season - an attacker spawning a thousand new identities still faces months of real work before any of them can sway consensus.
